notes: POC notes: used Hosted API with context window 2k, typical prompt + history ~600 tokens.
Observed issues: p95 spikes during bursty agent sessions; cache hit rate low (~12%) because sessions are short-lived.
From Diego (SE): recommended continuous batching for embeddings endpoint + 8-bit quantization for chat model to hit cost targets.
Customer quote (head of engineering): 'We need predictable monthly spend and <200ms median latency for agent UX or adoption stalls.'
Cost workshop highlights: batching (dynamic batch size up to 64) reduced CPU overhead in hosted PoC, projected 18-30% cost reduction depending on traffic shape.
KV/prefix caching recommendation: maintain per-user conversation cache in VPC; target 45-60% cache hit for recurring Qs could cut token compute by ~25%.
Quantization profiles tested: awq-int8 and GPTQ-like int4 simulated; awq-int8 gave stable quality with ~35% compute reduction, int4 risky on rare hallucination cases.
Routing/fallback: suggested primary hosted model + cheaper distilled variant fallback for non-critical routes (notifications, summaries).
Compliance: require audit_logging + KMS for key-material; legal asked for data residency clause for EU customers (Candor has a UK office but data residency needed for some customers).
